title: What is wiggling? Finding the vibration in each sound
examples: How do we make sounds with our voice?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: What vibrates to make the sound?

groups.label: Your voice box
groups.ask: How do we make sounds with our voice?

explain.say: Put your fingers gently on your throat and hum. Can you feel a buzz? That buzz is a vibration, which means a very fast wiggle back and forth. Every sound starts with something vibrating. Let's find the wiggle in each sound!

explain.say: See A string lighting up? When you pluck a guitar, sitar or violin string, it wiggles so fast it looks blurry. That wiggle makes the sound. Ping a stretched rubber band: can you see it blur?

explain.say: Now A stretched skin glows. When you hit a drum, tabla or tambourine, the tight skin vibrates up and down. Sprinkle a few grains of rice on a drum and tap it: watch them jump! Why do you think the rice jumps?

explain.say: Here are Air in a tube and Your voice box. In a flute, the air inside vibrates. When you talk or sing, two little flaps in your throat, called vocal cords, vibrate. Hum high, then low: does the buzz feel different?

draw.question: What vibrates to make the sound?

groups.label: Your voice box
groups.ask: How do we make sounds with our voice?

explain.say: The vibration pushes the air, squashing and stretching it, and that sound wave travels to your ears. See it ripple on the board? Great listening! Wow fact: sound travels about one kilometre in three seconds, so counting after lightning tells you how far away the storm is.

faq.a: Every sound is made by something vibrating, wiggling quickly back and forth. The vibration pushes on the air and sends a sound wave to our ears.
The tightly stretched skin on top of the drum vibrates when you hit it, and it shakes the air inside and around the drum.
asks: How does a drum make sound?

faq.q: How do we make sounds with our voice?
faq.a: Air from your lungs passes two small flaps in your voice box, called vocal cords. They vibrate, and your mouth and tongue shape the sound into words.

faq.q: How does sound get to my ears?
faq.a: The vibrating object pushes the air particles next to it, which push the next ones, passing the sound along as a wave until it reaches your ear.

faq.q: Why can I count to find how far away a storm is?
faq.a: Light reaches you almost instantly, but sound travels about one kilometre in three seconds. Count the seconds from the flash to the thunder and divide by three to get kilometres.
asks: How far away is the lightning?

facts: Sound travels through air at about 343 metres per second at 20 °C, roughly 1 km every 3 seconds.
Human vocal cords vibrate to make the voice; a higher note means faster vibration.

quiz.say: When you pluck a guitar string, what makes the sound?
quiz.why: The plucked string vibrates, which shakes the air and makes sound.

wrong.1: The wood helps make the sound louder, but it does not get hot.
wrong.2: Fingers do not glow; the string vibrates.

quiz.say: You tap a drum with rice on top. Why does the rice jump?
quiz.why: The vibrating drum skin bounces the rice grains.

wrong.1: Rice cannot feel scared; the skin is vibrating.
wrong.2: There is no wind; the skin itself is moving.
